text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
LIETUVOS RYTAS
- The board of the Bank of Lithuania imposed restrictions on the activities of Tauras Bank and removed the chairman of the bank and its board.

- The three prime ministers of the Baltic countries made an oral statement about their readiness to join European Union but a different approch on tactics prevented the signing of a joint written declaration planned earlier.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius opposed a suggestion by the finance ministry to issue state guarantees for $200 million of credits to finance the building of the Butinge oil terminal.
- Official list company Rokishkis Cheese signed an agreement with Vilfima and Williams de Broe over placing its shares abroad in the form of global depository receipts (GDRs).
RESPUBLIKA
- Explosives were discovered under a car owned by an Israeli due to testify in an oil smuggling case.
- A Chechen parliament delegation arrived in Vilnius. They brought a letter from the country's president, Aslan Maschadov, with an appeal to recognise Checnya as an independent state.
- The chairman of the state-run Lithuanian Savings Bank wrote a letter of resignation over planned changes in the bank's administration.
LIETUVOS AIDAS
- The board of Tauras Bank admitted to the Bank of Lithuania that it saw little possibility of being saved from financial crisis.
- The demarcation of the Lithuania-Belarus border has started.
- Every second audio cassette and eight out of 10 CDs sold in Lithuania are pirated versions, record companies said.
VERSLO ZINIOS

- Five months into the year, the leaders of the banking sector have not changed and the laggards have become more apparent. Litimpex, Tauras and Agriculture Bank have failed to meet the capital adequacy requirements of the central bank.
- Hermis Bank reported a 13.8 million litas net profit for the first five months of the year and targets 40.6 million litas net profit for 1997.
- Neste doubts if it will succeed in opening 30 filling stations by 2000 due to a state policy of protectionism.

- Market research agency the Social Information Centre said that the television advertising by Utenos beer, Kalnapilis beer, Always feminine hygiene products, Jacobs coffee and Blend-a-Med were most successful.
- Ignalina nuclear power plant produced 5.919 billion kilowatt hours in the first five months of the year.
-- Andrius Vilkancas, Vilnius newsroom +370 2 22 35 17
